name: Grant exception dossier preparation
why: Recommendations that fail the board-adopted deterministic policy (nonstandard grantee, purpose, benefit or conflict flags) need a checked dossier before an accountable sponsor official decides
staffing_note: Scales with grants x exception intensity; AI drafts and a human checks; first activity to exceed founder capacity in T/F

name: Grant exception decision by authorized sponsor official
why: IRC 4966(d)(2) exclusive legal control and CNV-GRT-001: exceptions are individual accountable decisions; AI is prohibited from deciding
staffing_note: Sponsor-borne in every model; never an Echelon Foundry role (CNV-GOV-004)

name: Routine grant approval (policy-conforming grants)
why: Exists only if the sponsor has not adopted a deterministic grant policy (CNV-GRT-001); once adopted, routine grants execute on policy and humans sample post hoc
staffing_note: Sponsor-borne; base assumes policy adopted with 10% post-hoc sampling, high end assumes every grant individually approved

name: Charity eligibility exception preparation
why: New, renamed, foreign, fiscally sponsored or mismatched organizations cannot be resolved from authoritative IRS data alone
staffing_note: Change-driven design removes routine re-vetting; residual is genuinely ambiguous identity or status

name: Charity eligibility determination
why: Taxable-expenditure exposure under IRC 4966 rests with the sponsor, which must decide ambiguous eligibility
staffing_note: Sponsor-borne in every model

name: Change-driven re-vetting of active grantees
why: Eligibility-relevant registry changes (revocation, status or name changes) affecting a sponsor's grantees; revocation applies a hold deterministically and only ambiguous cases reach a person
staffing_note: 405 of 236,750 monthly BMF changes were eligibility-relevant (charity-network 02:139)

name: 180-day deep-review renewal (ceiling retained)
why: OD-CDD-02 approval: change-driven renewal within the retained 180-day ceiling with evidence freshness checks; humans only where evidence is incomplete
staffing_note: SPW-051: 120k reviews at 100k accounts, 10 min conventional vs 0.2 expected minimum-touch

name: Contribution attribution exceptions
why: Pooled or unidentified receipts (checks, securities without fund reference) must be attributed to the right fund before acknowledgment
staffing_note: Prevented by notification-first intents and fund references; residual 2-10% of contributions

name: Contribution posting exceptions
why: Noncash, mismatched or late-dated contributions need a human posting check (four contribution dates, CNV-FIN-003)
staffing_note: Scales with contributions x exception intensity

name: Payment exception preparation
why: Payments that fail deterministic checks (destination change, threshold, rail failure) need preparation for sponsor release
staffing_note: Rails are sponsor pass-through; Unbound never executes a payment (CNV-LEG-001)

name: Payment batch release under dual control
why: CNV-GOV-003: distinct sponsor persons release payments (three until the deterministic gate is auditor- and board-accepted; then two)
staffing_note: Sponsor-borne in every model; EF may not be Originator or operator (UNB-CDD-CMF-005)

name: Payment failures (returns uncashed voids reissue)
why: Returned ACH and uncashed checks require reissue or escheat handling
staffing_note: Verified destinations and positive pay reduce frequency

name: Reconciliation break investigation
why: Daily automated matching leaves breaks that a person must explain (CNV-FIN-004)
staffing_note: Single ledger with continuous reconciliation; breaks ~1-2%

name: Monthly close preparation
why: Each sponsor's books close monthly; preparation is performed outside the payment chain
staffing_note: E13: 9,000 native vs 28,800 conventional minutes per sponsor-year

name: Monthly reconciliation review and controller sign-off
why: CNV-GOV-003 / CNV-FIN-004: independent review at least monthly and controller sign-off by the sponsor
staffing_note: Sponsor-borne control; never modelled away

name: Sanctions alert triage preparation
why: Screening hits that the tuned matcher cannot clear need a human comparison
staffing_note: 0.9 alerts per 1000 names with the token matcher vs 10.5 naive

name: OFAC true-match blocking and reporting decision
why: 31 CFR 501 blocking and reporting obligations fall on the sponsor as a US person
staffing_note: Rare; sponsor-borne

name: Donor and advisor support contacts
why: Donors and advisors ask about grants, statements and access; self-service and proactive status remove most contacts
staffing_note: Only full-service administration puts donor contacts on Echelon Foundry; first hire trigger in F at scale

name: Sponsor-staff product support (tier 2)
why: Sponsor staff report defects and ask product questions; partner channels take front line (W)
staffing_note: Contract-typical response times; founder covers at low counts

name: Statement and acknowledgment exceptions
why: Section 170(f)(8)/(18) acknowledgments and statements that fail validation
staffing_note: Generated deterministically; exceptions only

name: Account opening and change exceptions
why: Identity mismatch or sensitive changes requiring step-up review
staffing_note: Prefill and step-up authentication remove most

name: Succession case preparation
why: Death or incapacity triggers verified successor handling
staffing_note: Rare; human by nature

name: Successor approval
why: Successor privileges are created only on sponsor approval
staffing_note: Sponsor-borne

name: Fraud investigation (account takeover payment redirection)
why: Nacha false-pretenses monitoring and destination evidence (TPSP obligations)
staffing_note: Rare; specialist

name: Complex and noncash gift acceptance
why: Gift acceptance policy and qualified appraisal decisions belong to the sponsor
staffing_note: Sponsor-borne

name: Account closure exceptions
why: Final grants or transfers needing review
staffing_note: Rare

name: Board and regulatory reporting preparation
why: Schedule D and Form 990 DAF inputs, board reporting
staffing_note: Annual per sponsor

name: Sponsor financial audit (sponsor side)
why: Each sponsor's annual audit; evidence-by-default narrows but does not remove it
staffing_note: Held at conventional minutes (Phase II CHL-105)

name: Auditor support from Echelon Foundry
why: Walkthroughs, PBC requests and SOC report bridging for each sponsor's auditor
staffing_note: Grows with customers; a SOC report reduces per-customer effort

name: Sponsor-reserved policy and oversight
why: Board policy adoption, delegation and committee oversight reserved to the sponsor
staffing_note: Borne by the sponsor in every model (Phase II PAR-013)

name: Customer onboarding and configuration
why: Tenant set-up, policy configuration, integration and parallel run for each new customer
staffing_note: E23 one-time 18,000 native minutes; the dominant per-new-customer cost

name: Configuration upkeep
why: Policy and configuration changes requested by the sponsor
staffing_note: Sponsor self-serves under licensing

name: Migration project (fixed)
why: Source-system extraction, mapping, rehearsal and reconciliation-gated cutover (Transitus)
staffing_note: Project work; contractors absorb peaks

name: Migration per-account validation
why: Per-account mapping and reconciliation exceptions
staffing_note: All accounts are migrating under model M

name: Incident response (platform-wide)
why: Production incidents must be detected and resolved within declared objectives
staffing_note: Requires on-call coverage (COV-ONC)

name: Incident response (customer-specific)
why: Tenant-specific issues grow with customers
staffing_note: Grows with customers

name: Change authoring and release management
why: Control-module changes need two non-author approvers (CNV-PLT-010); this is the author's time
staffing_note: Reviewer time is purchased through COV-CHG

name: Security operations
why: Patching, vulnerability triage, quarterly access reviews, key rotation, log review

name: Backup restore and DR class tests
why: Annual restore test per data class and isolation profile (RR-UNB-RES-003-r1); semi-annual per work inventory
staffing_note: Contradiction annual vs semi-annual carried as the rate range

name: Per-tenant restore test with key-rotation evidence
why: CNV-ARC-005: each tenant restore-tested at least annually
staffing_note: Grows with customers

name: SOC 2 evidence and audit liaison
why: Continuous evidence collection and annual audit fieldwork
staffing_note: Automation platform reduces but does not remove

name: SOC 1 evidence (user-auditor reliance)
why: CNV-GOV-001: SOC 1 Type 2 when a user auditor relies on Unbound controls; mandatory before the first staffed (OD-M-08) client
staffing_note: Only where EF performs controls

name: Charity and sanctions data pipeline stewardship
why: IRS BMF, Pub 78, revocation, 990-N, 990 e-file and OFAC connectors with archive and freshness alarms
staffing_note: Phase II RC-06: 400 h connector maintenance; free sources

name: Maintenance engineering (platform)
why: Dependencies, defects, tax-year and Nacha rule changes, browser and API deprecations
staffing_note: Largest fixed engineering load

name: Maintenance engineering (customer-specific)
why: Integrations, configuration defects, customer-requested fixes
staffing_note: Grows with customers

name: December readiness and load test
why: UNB-AVL-013: load test before each December (3x surge)
staffing_note: Annual

name: Monitoring and alert triage
why: Non-incident alerts and capacity checks
staffing_note: Tuning reduces

name: Vendor assurance and policy upkeep
why: CNV-GOV-002 annual vendor-assurance review; policy maintenance
ef_models: L W T F C M
staffing_note: Founder-held

name: National registry change review (charity intelligence)
why: Review of eligibility-relevant IRS changes nationally (~405/month) before publishing to subscribers
staffing_note: Fixed regardless of subscribers

name: Source-rights and licensing review
why: Non-redistributable sources must stay out of shared stores (UNB-CNET-011); counsel questions remain open
staffing_note: Founder-held

name: Charity intelligence subscriber support
why: Subscriber questions and disputes about published status
staffing_note: Grows with subscribers

name: Charity intelligence pipeline and API maintenance (standalone product)
why: A standalone registry product needs its own publishing API and pipeline upkeep; the full Unbound platform is not required
staffing_note: Replaces ACT-PLT-10 for model C
